holidays.name: National Cotton Candy Day
holidays.description: A fluffy, sugary celebration of spun sugar. Grab a cloud of pink or blue and let it dissolve on your tongue at the fair, the boardwalk, or your own kitchen counter.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and the exact origin of the day is unclear. It honors the carnival treat that became widely popular in the early 1900s.
holidays.funFact: Cotton candy was introduced to a wide audience at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair. A dentist, William Morrison, helped invent the machine that made it.

holidays.name: National Letter Writing Day
holidays.description: A day to put down the phone and pick up a pen. Write a handwritten note to a friend, relative, or someone you've been meaning to thank, and put a stamp on it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to keep the art of the handwritten letter alive.
holidays.funFact: Letters were once the main way people stayed in touch over long distances. Some famous correspondences, like those of the poet Emily Dickinson, are now studied as literature.

holidays.name: International Civil Aviation Day
holidays.description: A day recognizing the role of air travel in connecting people and economies around the world. It is a good moment to appreciate pilots, air traffic controllers, and ground crews.
holidays.origin: The International Civil Aviation Organization was established in 1944 when the Convention on International Civil Aviation was signed in Chicago on December 7. The day has been observed since 1994 and was later recognized by the United Nations.
holidays.funFact: The Chicago Convention of 1944 set the rules for international air travel that are still in use today, including the principle that every country controls the airspace above its own territory.
